excerpt: When faced with a case in which it seems that [p] is fully grounded in D yet ~0(∧D → p), the advocate of necessity should check to see if there are additional explanatorily relevant facts P such that 0(∧(D, P) → p). If such additional facts are available, we have reason to believe that D is a mere partial ground that was misidentified as a full ground; in such a case, [p] instead is fully grounded in D, P.
overview: This passage gives the paper's method for handling apparent failures of necessity. It does not deny the intuitions behind counterexamples outright; it asks whether the proposed ground is incomplete and whether adding explanatorily relevant facts restores entailment.
title: Counterexample Diagnostic
